instantiated_cells.justification: Section 86117(a) requires reports to be filed during the month following each calendar quarter, not annually.
Section 86117(a) specifies quarterly reporting (filed the month after each calendar quarter), not monthly reporting.
The statute prescribes quarterly periodic reports and does not provide an alternative 'other' reporting frequency option for principals.
Persons described in §86115 must file periodic reports under §86116, and §86117(a) requires those reports be filed during the month following each calendar quarter.
Section 86117(a) sets quarterly filing, not semi-annual filing.
Section 86117(a) ties reporting to calendar quarters rather than a tri-annual legislative calendar schedule.

The periodic report must include the filer’s identifying information and 'a description of the specific lobbying interests of the filer,' which entails describing the filer’s nature/interests (business) in the report context.

Section 86116 requires reporting 'the total amount of payments to each lobbying firm' and 'the total amount of all payments to lobbyists employed by the filer,' which are direct lobbying compensation costs.
Section 86116 lists required contents of the principal’s periodic report and does not require disclosure of specific lobbying contacts or communications.
Section 86116(d) requires 'a description of the specific lobbying interests of the filer,' which is disclosure of the issues lobbied in general terms.
Section 86116(f) requires reporting each 'activity expense' of the filer, and §86111(a) defines activity expenses to include gifts and other benefits.
Section 86116(h)(1) requires reporting 'the total of all other payments to influence legislative or administrative action including overhead expenses,' capturing indirect non-compensation costs.
Section 86116(b) requires only the 'total amount of payments to each lobbying firm' and does not require disclosure of contracted lobbyists’ addresses and phone numbers in the spending report.

The report must include periodic reports of each employed lobbyist, but §86116 does not require the principal to list by name all lobbyists representing it (including those at contracted firms) in the spending report.
Section 86116 does not require disclosure of major financial contributors to the principal.
Section 86116(a) requires the filer’s 'business address, and telephone number' in the periodic report.
Section 86116(d) requires a description of specific lobbying interests but does not require identifying specific bills or legislation IDs.

Section 86116 requires totals for payments to each lobbying firm and to employed lobbyists plus 'all other payments to influence' legislative/administrative action, together covering total lobbying expenditures across in-house and contract activity.
The principal must report total payments to each lobbying firm and total payments to employed lobbyists, which includes salary/fees paid to lobbyists.
Payments to lobbying firms, employed lobbyists, and other lobbying-related payments are reported as totals rather than itemized by transaction in §86116.
Section 86116 contains no requirement that associations or representative groups disclose names of all sponsors or members in the periodic spending report.
Section 86116(e) requires including 'a periodic report completed and verified by each lobbyist employed by a lobbyist employer,' which entails identifying the employed lobbyists in the filing.
